title: Land at Neko Harbour and climb the marked snow ridge
description: Make an expedition-supervised continental landing, then follow the guided or marked snow route to the rocky overlook while staying ready to clear the beach if glacier calving sends waves ashore.

title: Sail the ice-choked Lemaire Channel
description: Watch the cliffs of Booth Island and the Peninsula close around the ship through this narrow west-coast passage, understanding that ice can force the expedition leader to turn back or reroute.

title: Post a card from Port Lockroy's living museum
description: On a scheduled expedition landing, step into Bransfield House's seasonal museum and post office to see early polar-science artefacts and support the heritage trust that conserves the site.

title: Visit Damoy Hut and trace Antarctica's former air link
description: Join a permission-cleared heritage landing at the former British air-transit hut, inspect its preserved interior in a small group and view the old skiway landscape without venturing onto the crevassed glacier.

title: Enter Base W's time capsule on Detaille Island
description: When ice, weather and prior permission align on a far-south voyage, land on slippery rock and enter the shuttered 1950s base in a closely supervised group, leaving every artefact untouched.

title: Join a permitted visit to Scott's Terra Nova hut
place: Scott's Terra Nova hut at Cape Evans
description: If the expedition's permits, sea ice and weather align, a trained guide may lead small groups through Scott's 1911 base and its artefact landscape. Hut entry needs a key and is never guaranteed; the nearby Magnetic Hut is closed.

title: Seek a landing beside Antarctica's first expedition huts
description: A rare small-boat landing may reach the 1899 Southern Cross base on Ridley Beach, where the first buildings erected on the continent stand among historic stores. Permit, guide and key are required, while nesting penguins and fast-changing ice can restrict or cancel access.

title: Walk the sea ice toward Snow Hill's emperor colony
description: Join a specialist ship-and-helicopter attempt to reach the emperor penguin colony, then walk across sea ice from a landing point kept safely away from the birds. Sea-ice thickness, weather and wildlife welfare decide whether the colony can be reached.

title: Trace Paulet Island's guided hut-and-volcano route
description: If ice, tide and nesting Adélies allow a landing, walk in a tightly managed small group toward the 1903 stone hut and volcanic lake. There is no free roaming: changing colony distribution can shorten the route or turn the visit into a small-boat viewing instead.

title: Climb Devil Island's flagged south-peak trail
description: From a conditions-dependent small-boat landing, follow the single flagged track above Devil Island's twin volcanic cones to a Weddell Sea viewpoint. The steep ridge, shifting pack ice, reefs and penguin traffic require close expedition-guide control and can make the longer walk unavailable.
